\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{साफ़} \hi{करना}}
\textbf{\hi{साफ़} \hi{करना}} — \emph{sāf karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to clean\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{साफ़} \hi{करना}} (\emph{sāf karnā}) is \emph{sāf}, \textquotedblleft{}clean\textquotedblright{}, from Arabic \emph{ṣāfī}, \textquotedblleft{}pure\textquotedblright{}, through Persian (Lane, root \emph{ṣ-f-w}), with the inherited \emph{karnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\hi{पोंछना} (põchnā)}{पोंछना (põchnā)}]{\hi{पोंछना} (põchnā) — to wipe}

\label{lesson:HI-C225-pochna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Hindi for to clean, then the Hindi for to dust.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \hi{पोंछना}}
\textbf{\hi{पोंछना}} — \emph{põchnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to wipe\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\hi{पोंछना}} (\emph{põchnā}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited from Sanskrit and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{proñchati}, \textquotedblleft{}wipes off\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9011). CDIAL suggests that the Sanskrit word itself was made over from a Middle Indo-Aryan \emph{*poṁch-}.
\end{cousinweb}
